entries.exactPassage: Here’s the tension: money flows from perceived value, not necessarily real value. Things that look valuable attract money — even when they are not. Things that are genuinely valuable but invisible do not attract money. The farmer who grows food and the marketer who sells the brand are both creating value — but only one is visible. Visibility is a form of value. You must learn to make your value seen without pretending it is something it is not.
entries.concern: A farmer can be visible and a marketer invisible; perceived value and compensation do not measure all social contribution.
entries.proposedWording: Both the farmer and marketer may contribute. Some contributions are less visible or less fairly rewarded than others; price alone does not show their full value.

entries.exactPassage: The extra mile is never crowded. Most people do exactly what they are paid for, exactly what is expected, and not one thing more. That is not laziness. That is self-protection. The people who give the extra effort, the extra attention, the extra care — they are the ones who get noticed, who get promoted, who get opportunities. Not because the world is fair. entries.exactPassage: You are the average of the people you spend the most time with. That is not a metaphor. It is a psychological reality. Their beliefs become your beliefs. Their habits become your habits. Their fears become your fears. This is not their fault. It is not your fault. It is how humans are wired. But here is the tension: you cannot always choose who is in your inner circle. You cannot choose your family. You cannot always choose your classmates. What you can choose is who you pay attention to. What you can choose is whose voice you amplify in your own mind. What you can choose is who you seek out for wisdom, even if they are in your outer circle. You cannot control who surrounds you. But you can control who influences you. That difference is the difference between being shaped by accident and being shaped by intention.
entries.concern: An average-of-people claim is presented as psychological law. Influence is variable, not deterministic.
entries.proposedWording: People around you can influence your beliefs and habits. The strength and direction of that influence vary; they do not determine your future.
